upg6:1.1: Recollection of the Buddha, friendliness, unattractiveness, and mindfulness of death -
upg6:1.2: these are the four protective meditations that a virtuous monk should develop.
upg6:2.1: Recollecting the Sage’s virtue, and his endless, extensive, good qualities,
upg6:2.2: the wise monk should develop the recollection of the Buddha first.
upg6:4.1: Alone he destroyed all the corruptions, and (bad) predispositions,
upg6:4.2: and being continually and fully pure he is worthy of worship at all times.
upg6:5.1: ° The Sage by himself has, in every way, completely awakened to all things
upg6:5.2: throughout the whole of time, and alone he has arrived at omniscience.
upg6:6.1: ° Being endowed with great psychic power, good conduct, virtue, and so on,
upg6:6.2: true understanding, insight, and so on, the leader was like the shining sky.
upg6:7.1: He who never spoke foolish words, has arrived at that glorious state (Nibbāna),
upg6:7.2: he knew the threefold world system (completely) without leaving anything out.
upg6:8.1: Overflowing with countless good qualities he is supreme among all beings,
upg6:8.2: with countless skilful means he tamed those men who could be tamed.
upg6:9.1: He alone, to the whole world was the teacher of everything good,
upg6:9.2: he is the highest treasure, having qualities such as good fortune, mastery, and so on.
upg6:10.1: Being wise in regard to all things compassionate to everybody,
upg6:10.2: he exceeded (others) in the best qualities, (knowing) what was for his own and others’ good.
upg6:11.1: Through sympathy he set his mind on the perfections through wisdom he raised himself up,
upg6:11.2: he raised himself above all things, through sympathy he raised others too.
upg6:12.1: Even his visible form-body was beyond thought,
upg6:12.2: what can be said of his spiritual body, which was unique, having powerful knowledge?
upg6:14.1: In a similar way to oneself, all beings desire happiness,
upg6:14.2: having seen that one should gradually develop friendliness towards all beings.
upg6:15.1: May I constantly be happy, free from suffering, and like myself
upg6:15.2: may my benefactors be happy, neutral persons, and foes also.
upg6:16.1: In this village, and its surrounding fields, may beings always be happy,
upg6:16.2: and those in other countries, and people throughout the universe.
upg6:17.1: ° Throughout the entire universe may the countless beings, creatures,
upg6:17.2: persons, and bhūtas, who have attained individuality, be happy,
upg6:18.1: and so too (all) women, men, noble ones, and also ignoble ones,
upg6:18.2: gods, humans, and fallen creatures, and likewise (all beings) in the ten directions.
upg6:20.1: With consciousness it is unattractive, just as it is without (i.e. dead),
upg6:20.2: seeing this body as unattractive, a monk should develop (the recollection) of the unattractive.
upg6:21.1: Thus by way of colour, shape, smell, location, and appearance,
upg6:21.2: the thirty-two (parts) in my body (are like) repulsive corpses.
upg6:22.1: The (parts) that depend on this body are contemptible, as is what falls from a corpse,
upg6:22.2: for their receptacle is impure, they are situated in this corpse of a body.
upg6:23.1: Like a worm in excrement this body arose in what is impure (i.e. the womb),
upg6:23.2: inside it is full of impurities just like a full lavatory.
upg6:24.1: Always the impurities overflow like fat (overflows) from a frying pan,
upg6:24.2: various kinds of worms dwell in it, the same as in a cesspool.
upg6:25.1: This bodily heap is like a boil, like a disease, or like a sore,
upg6:25.2: it is incurable, contemptible, just like a rotting corpse.
upg6:27.1: By comparing a lamp in a breeze, with the destruction of the life continuum,
upg6:27.2: through seeing oneself as similar to others, one should develop mindfulness of death.
upg6:28.1: Just as people who have attained great good fortune here have died,
upg6:28.2: in the same way will I die death is (surely) coming to me.
upg6:29.1: Indeed death always comes along with that which has arisen,
upg6:29.2: it is like a murderer who is seeking an opportunity to kill.
upg6:30.1: ° This life is slowly, without turning back, continually, eagerly,
upg6:30.2: going its way, it rises and falls just as the sun runs its course (and sets).
upg6:31.1: (Like) lightning, a bubble, dew, a line drawn on water, life (quickly goes to) destruction,
upg6:31.2: like an executioner in regard to his rival (death) can never be constrained.
upg6:32.1: Even the two kinds of Victors, who are famous, strong, meritorious, powerful, and of great intelligence,
upg6:32.2: were quickly slaughtered by death, so what to say about one like me?
upg6:33.1: When conditions fail there are internal and external adversities,
upg6:33.2: dying at each and every moment I will die in less (time) than a blink of an eye.
upg6:35.1: Having developed these four protections one should consider next
upg6:35.2: the eight great bases for urgency, having non-stop energy.
upg6:36.1: Birth, old age, sickness, death, the lower realms,
upg6:36.2: the past and future suffering in the round,
upg6:36.3: the suffering in having to seek food in the present -
upg6:36.4: these are the eight bases for urgency.
upg6:37.1: If, in the morning and in the evening, one who knows the way,
upg6:37.2: who desires his own benefit, practises (these meditations) continually,
upg6:37.3: ° then after destroying (even) extensive obstacles, that sage
upg6:37.4: easily attains great happiness, and the distinction of the deathless.
